news.Title: Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Analysis
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . A Closer Look at the Upcoming Payout, Dividend History, and Growth Outlook for the Semiconductor Leader Texas Instruments Inc ( NASDAQ:TXN ) recently announced a total dividend of $1.52 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-10-30. This amount consists of a $1.52 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-11-10. For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a key marker: shareholders must own the stock before that date to qualify for the payment. As investors look forward to this upcoming distribution, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Texas Instruments Inc's dividend performance and assess its sustainability. What Does Texas Instruments Inc Do? Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TXN. High Yield Dividend Stocks in Gurus' Portfolio This Powerful Chart Made Peter Lynch 29% A Year For 13 Years How to calculate the intrinsic value of a stock? Is TXN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures semiconductors sold to electronics designers and manufacturers worldwide, generating $17.68 billion of revenue in 2025. Its Analog segment (about 79% of revenue) supplies power management and signal chain chips that condition, amplify, convert, and manage electrical signals and power in nearly every type of electronic equipment; its Embedded Processing segment provides microcontrollers and processors. TI's portfolio exceeds 80,000 products serving industrial, automotive, personal electronics, data center, and communications markets, sold largely through its own direct channel. Its competitive advantages include internal manufacturing and technology, highlighted by a multi-year investment cycle in 300-millimeter wafer fabs in Texas and Utah, portfolio breadth, channel reach, and product longevity. Founded in 1930 and headquartered in Dallas, TI manages the business to maximize long-term free cash flow per share. A Glimpse at Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend History Texas Instruments Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 1985, and dividends are currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2001. The stock is thus listed as a dividend aristocrat, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 25 years. For value investors, such a long record signals disciplined capital allocation and a management team committed to returning cash to shareholders through complete business cycles. Story Continues Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share for tracking historical trends. Breaking Down Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth As of today, Texas Instruments Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 2.04%. The gap between the two suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. The trailing yield reflects dividends actually paid over the past year, while the forward yield incorporates the most recent dividend rate annualized, so a higher forward figure implies the payout has recently been raised. Over the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 5.50%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate increased to 8.00% per year. And over the past decade, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 15.20%. This pattern of decelerating growth from the 10-year to the 3-year window is worth noting: it may reflect a more mature payout policy or a period of heavier capital investment in manufacturing capacity. Based on Texas Instruments Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Texas Instruments Inc stock as of today is approximately 2.82%. Yield on cost estimates the effective return on today's investment after five years of assumed dividend growth, offering a forward-looking complement to the current yield. The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-09-30, Texas Instruments Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.73. And this may suggest that the company's dividend may not be sustainable, since a ratio approaching three-quarters of earnings leaves a narrower cushion for reinvestment and adverse conditions. Texas Instruments Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Texas Instruments Inc's profitability 8 out of 10 as of 2026-09-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported positive net income for each year over the past decade, further solidifying its high profitability. This earnings consistency is an important counterweight when judging whether the current payout level can be maintained. Growth Metrics: The Future Outlook To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Texas Instruments Inc's growth rank of 8 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. However, the headline rank should be read alongside the underlying operating trends discussed below, which have been uneven in recent years amid a cyclical semiconductor downturn and heavy capital spending. Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Texas Instruments Inc's revenue per share , combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate , indicates a strong revenue model. Texas Instruments Inc's revenue has increased by approximately -3.60% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 63.15% of global competitors. The negative figure reflects the recent industry correction rather than a structural loss of demand, but it does temper the growth picture. The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's earnings increased by approximately -16.80% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 67.5% of global competitors. Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of -6.00% underperforms approximately 69.47% of global competitors. Next Steps for Dividend-Focused Investors Texas Instruments Inc's dividend story is one of strong foundations and near-term tension. On the positive side, the company has paid dividends since 1985, raised them every year since 2001, and holds dividend aristocrat status, backed by a profitability rank of 8 out of 10 and a decade of positive net income. The forward yield of 2.04% exceeding the trailing 1.92% points to continued increases, and a 5-year yield on cost of roughly 2.82% rewards patient holders. Yet a payout ratio of 0.73, combined with negative three-year revenue and EPS growth and a -6.00% five-year EBITDA trend, suggests the dividend consumes a meaningful share of earnings during the current downturn. For value investors, the key question is whether Texas Instruments Inc's long-term free cash flow per share can resume growth as analog demand recovers and the 300-millimeter fab investment cycle matures. A payout ratio near 0.73 is not alarming for a cyclical semiconductor leader, but it warrants monitoring alongside cash flow rather than earnings alone. Readers should watch upcoming quarterly reports for signs of revenue stabilization and capital spending discipline. news.Title: Brokers Suggest Investing in Texas Instruments (TXN): Read This Before Placing a Bet
news.Content:
Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Texas Instruments (TXN) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Texas Instruments currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.93, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 33 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.93 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 33 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 19 are Strong Buy, representing 57.6% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for TXN

Check price target & stock forecast for Texas Instruments here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Texas Instruments, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

It has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts issue more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them.

On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Is TXN Worth Investing In?

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Texas Instruments, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 5.6% over the past month to $8.89.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for Texas Instruments. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for Texas Instruments may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: Vicor Stock is Overvalued at 16.52X EV/Sales: Should You Still Buy it?
news.Content:
Vicor VICR shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. In terms of the trailing 12-month EV/Sales, VICR is trading at 16.52X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 8.19X. The company is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Analog Devices ' ADI 15.17X and Texas Instruments ' TXN 13.82X, but cheaper than Monolithic Power Systems ' MPWR 17.76X.

Vicor's Shares Trade at a Premium

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is Vicor worth buying at current prices? Let us dig deep to find out.

VICR Shares Ride on AI Prospects

Year to date (YTD), Vicor shares have outperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, as well as Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments. Vicor returned a whopping 93.4% YTD while the broader sector, Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments have returned 14.9%, 33.7%, 54.3% and 78%, respectively.

Vicor Stock's Price Performance

Vicor is benefiting from increasing demand for high-density power delivery solutions as AI processors require greater power efficiency and higher current density. The company's second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology is emerging as a key growth catalyst. VICR claims that its proprietary all-FPA technology can reduce AI processor power losses by 10-15%, while delivering more than 40 times the current gain of integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and three times the current density of conventional voltage regulators. These advantages are expected to strengthen Vicor's competitive position as next-generation AI processors become increasingly power-intensive.

The company's expanding royalty business has been a key catalyst. In the third quarter of 2026, royalty revenues surged to $66.6 million from $21.7 million in the year-ago quarter. Vicor secured its first VPD license with a leading AI original equipment manufacturer and received licensing inquiries from two hyperscalers. The company expects royalty revenues of at least $43 million in the fourth quarter, even without additional licensing agreements. Further adoption of its patented technologies could create a growing, high-margin revenue stream, although quarterly royalty collections may remain uneven.

Manufacturing expansion represents another important long-term catalyst for the company. Vicor has acquired two additional sites for ChiP Fab-2 and ChiP Fab-3, potentially increasing total manufacturing capacity to nearly five times that of Fab-1. Initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 is expected in the second quarter of 2027. This expansion should help address production bottlenecks, support rising customer demand and unlock additional revenue opportunities.

Story Continues

VICR Benefits From Strong ATE Business & Balance Sheet

Vicor's growth opportunities also extend beyond AI processors. Strong demand for automatic test equipment (ATE) used in ASIC and memory testing is supporting the company's business, with leading ATE customers generating more than $100 million in annual revenues. VICR is also witnessing opportunities in industrial, aerospace and defense markets, particularly from emerging companies developing autonomous technologies. These diversified growth drivers should reduce dependence on any single application and support sustained demand for the company's power solutions.

Vicor's strong balance sheet further supports its long-term expansion plans. The company ended September 2026 with $513.1 million in cash and cash equivalents. VICR expects to finance Fab-2 and eventually Fab-3 without raising additional capital. Improving operating cash generation and increased production scale should strengthen the company' ability to fund innovation, expand manufacturing and capitalize on emerging growth opportunities.

Vicor's 2026 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.94 per share, up 8% over the past 30 days, suggesting 51% growth from the 2025 reported figure.

Vicor Corporation Price and Consensus

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.13 per share, down by four cents over the past 30 days and indicating 12% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Despite its premium valuation and impressive YTD rally, Vicor remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by strong AI-driven demand, expanding royalty revenues and growing adoption of second-generation VPD technology. The company's manufacturing expansion, solid backlog and strong balance sheet further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Although elevated valuation and near-term capacity constraints remain concerns, VICR's technological leadership and expanding growth opportunities justify its premium and make the stock worth considering for long-term investors.

Vicor currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: TXN's Gross Margin Crosses 64% in Q3: Can It Improve Further?
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN delivered a strong improvement in profitability in the third quarter of 2026, raising hopes that its gross margin can climb further. The semiconductor maker reported a gross margin of 64.2%, up from 57.4% in the year-ago quarter and 61.4% in the previous quarter.

Texas Instruments' third-quarter gross profit rose 43% year over year to $3.89 billion, outpacing the 28% increase in revenues to $6.06 billion. Higher sales volumes supported the improvement, while better factory utilization, pricing and product mix also helped. These trends suggest that stronger demand can translate into better profitability when production facilities operate more efficiently.

Growth across key markets offers additional support. Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year, while automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens rate. Data center revenues surged about 95%, reflecting rising demand for chips used in expanding computing infrastructure. Continued strength in these markets could help TXN maintain higher production levels and spread manufacturing costs across more units.

Texas Instruments' 300-millimeter wafer manufacturing strategy could also support cost efficiency as output rises. Per the company, an unpackaged chip built on 300-millimeter wafers costs approximately 40% less than one built on 200-millimeter wafers. Texas Instruments has available cleanroom capacity in its Richardson, Sherman and Lehi facilities. Management plans to install additional equipment according to demand, supporting dependable supply and cost efficiency as production volumes increase.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues and earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 37.7% and 94.5%, respectively. These projections imply continued business activity, which could further expand Texas Instruments' margins.

How Do TXN's Competitors Compare on Gross Margin?

Analog Devices, Inc. ADI is a close competitor in analog chips and signal-processing technology. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI's revenues rose 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, while its GAAP gross margin increased to 67.3% from 62.1% in the year-ago quarter.

Its adjusted gross margin reached 72.5% from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter, highlighting strong profitability. These results put Analog Devices ahead of TXN's 64.2% gross margin.

Microchip Technology Incorporated MCHP is another competitor, supplying microcontrollers and embedded-control chips. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues grew 38% year over year to $1.49 billion.

Story Continues

Microchip Technology's GAAP gross margin improved to 63.2% from 53.6% in the year-ago quarter, while its non-GAAP gross margin reached 63.8% from 54.3%. Higher factory utilization and recovering demand supported the improvement.

Both companies show how stronger demand and manufacturing efficiency can lift margins. Analog Devices' higher reported margin sets a competitive benchmark, while Microchip Technology's performance highlights the benefits of better factory utilization.

TXN's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Texas Instruments have surged 78.1% year to date compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry's 22.6% growth.

Texas Instruments YTD Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, TXN trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 29.83, significantly higher than the industry's average of 16.66.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Texas Instruments' 2026 and 2027 earnings implies a year-over-year increase of 62.4% and 24.7%, respectively. Estimates for 2026 and 2027 have been revised upward over the past seven days.

Rosenblatt Securities' top pick is supported by several growth catalysts. TSMC's 2nm capacity is expected to double in 2027, which will support the ramp of AMD's Venice server CPU family. The firm views Venice as the market's highest-performing server CPU, featuring 16 memory channels compared to 12 in the prior generation. AMD CEO Lisa Su recently increased the projected 2030 server CPU total addressable market to $220 billion from $120 billion.

Meta's Muse and other emerging personal AI agents are driving server CPU demand, according to the firm. Rosenblatt notes that strong CPU demand and greater memory capacity create favorable conditions for the company. The firm's primary concern for data-center growth in 2027 and beyond is supply-chain capacity rather than demand weakness. Lam Research cited near-term supply constraints, while Texas Instruments highlighted extended lead times for back-end equipment.

However, Rosenblatt characterizes these as tactical challenges that the industry can address, rather than evidence of severe product shortages or weakening demand. The firm favors companies positioned to expand capacity and capture that demand.

news.Title: Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Texas Instruments Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
news.Content:
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Texas Instruments (TXN) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to TXN for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Texas Instruments' Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Texas Instruments' main business drivers.

Headquartered in Dallas, TX, Texas Instruments Incorporated is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.

Texas Instruments has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe.

Management's strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

In 2025, Texas Instruments generated total revenues of $17.68 billion, up 13% from 2024. The company has two reporting financial segments, Analog and Embedded Processing. It reports the results of its remaining business activities in Other.

Analog segment revenues grew 15% to $14.01 billion and accounted for approximately 79% of total revenues in 2025. Analog products have been categorized into two categories, Power and Signal Chain. Power products manage and distribute electricity, while Signal Chain products sense, condition and convert real-world signals.

Revenues from the Embedded Processing segment rose 6% to $2.70 billion and contributed approximately 15% to 2025 total revenues. This segment includes microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity and radar products.

The Other business generated $979 million in revenues and accounted for approximately 6% of 2025 total sales. The segment includes smaller product lines, such as DLP products, calculators and certain application-specific integrated circuits. Revenues from this segment increased 3% in 2025.

The company's products are sold in industrial, personal electronics, automotive, data center and communications equipment markets. In 2025, industrial and automotive each represented 33% of revenue. Personal electronics accounted for 21%, data center 9% and communications equipment 3%. Calculators represented about 1% of revenue.

Texas Instruments has more than 80,000 products and over 100,000 customers. In 2025, more than 80% of revenue was generated through direct sales channels.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio requires research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Texas Instruments, ten years ago, you're likely feeling pretty good about your investment today.

According to our calculations, a $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $4,157.30, or a gain of 315.73%, as of October 27, 2026, and this return excludes dividends but includes price increases.

Compare this to the S&P 500's rally of 258.82% and gold's return of 203.96% over the same time frame.

Analysts are anticipating more upside for TXN.

Texas Instruments is benefiting from a broad recovery in industrial and automotive demand and sustained data center expansion. Its analog and embedded portfolios serve diverse, long-lived applications. Internal manufacturing and growing capacity strengthen supply reliability while supporting margin recovery as utilization rises. Rising cash generation provides greater room for dividends and long-term investment. The planned Silicon Labs acquisition could extend its wireless connectivity reach. Management's outlook points to continued demand across its core markets. Semiconductor cyclicality, pricing competition, trade exposure and debt remain risks. Equipment delivery constraints could also slow capacity additions. Nonetheless, improving factory economics and a wider range of growth opportunities support an Outperform view.

The stock is up 7.12% over the past four weeks, and no earnings estimate has gone lower in the past two months, compared to 9 higher, for fiscal 2026. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

news.Title: Don't Overlook Texas Instruments (TXN) International Revenue Trends While Assessing the Stock
news.Content:
Have you assessed how the international operations of Texas Instruments (TXN) performed in the quarter ended September 2026? For this chipmaker, possessing an expansive global footprint, parsing the trends of international revenues could be critical to gauge its financial resilience and growth prospects.

In today's increasingly interconnected global economy, a company's ability to tap into international markets can be a pivotal factor in shaping its overall financial health and growth trajectory. For investors, understanding a company's reliance on overseas markets has become increasingly crucial, as it offers insights into the company's sustainability of earnings, ability to tap into diverse economic cycles and overall growth potential.

Being present in foreign markets serves as protection against local economic declines and helps benefit from more rapidly expanding economies. Yet, such expansion also introduces challenges related to currency fluctuations, geopolitical uncertainties and varied market behaviors.

While delving into TXN's performance for the past quarter, we observed some fascinating trends in the revenue from its foreign segments that are commonly modeled and observed by analysts on Wall Street.

The recent quarter saw the company's total revenue reaching $6.06 billion, marking an improvement of 27.7% from the prior-year quarter. Next, we'll examine the breakdown of TXN's revenue from abroad to comprehend the significance of its international presence.

A Look into TXN's International Revenue Streams

Of the total revenue, $104 million came from Rest of World during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 1.7%. This represented a surprise of -5.62% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $110.19 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $98 million, or 1.8%, and $74 million, or 1.6%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

During the quarter, Europe, Middle East and Africa contributed $1.21 billion in revenue, making up 19.9% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $1.24 billion, this meant a surprise of -2.52%. Looking back, Europe, Middle East and Africa contributed $1.08 billion, or 19.7%, in the previous quarter, and $972 million, or 20.5%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Japan generated $369 million in revenues for the company in the last quarter, constituting 6.1% of the total. This represented a surprise of -0.87% compared to the $372.23 million projected by Wall Street analysts. Comparatively, in the previous quarter, Japan accounted for $330 million (6%), and in the year-ago quarter, it contributed $313 million (6.6%) to the total revenue.

Story Continues

Rest of Asia accounted for 10.5% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $635 million. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of -1.4%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $644 million. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, Rest of Asia contributed $606 million (11.1%) and $505 million (10.7%) to the total revenue, respectively.

During the quarter, China contributed $1.39 billion in revenue, making up 23% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $1.28 billion, this meant a surprise of +8.77%.
